subject: SOC 2 evidence links for AWS/GCP Marketplace security review (what we can share + access controls)
body:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>; Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>; Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 28, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: SOC 2 evidence links for AWS/GCP Marketplace security review (what we can share + access controls)

Team —

Per PM-1847 and the partner feedback loop, we need a clean way to reference SOC 2 evidence for marketplace security review without oversharing (or posting anything publicly that should stay gated).

Ask:
1) Confirm what we are comfortable including directly in the AWS/GCP submission attachments vs “available on request”.
2) Confirm the access-control approach (who can grant, how we track, expiration, download controls).

I drafted an evidence index for marketplace reviewers (attached: SOC2-Marketplace-Evidence-Index-2026-01-28.xlsx). It’s split into:
- Public/OK-to-publish: security overview + shared responsibility + data handling/retention + audit log description
- Gated: SOC 2 Type II report + management assertion + bridge letter (if needed) + select policy excerpts
- On-request only: pen test executive summary, vulnerability mgmt evidence screenshots, IR tabletop artifacts

Also attached is a quick text file with the public links we can safely reference in listing/supporting docs.

Proposed approach (opinionated):
- Marketplace submission package includes: (a) security overview doc + (b) evidence index (no direct confidential URLs)
- For SOC 2 report: “available upon request” with access via our trust portal, time-bound, no public links

Questions to settle today:
- Do we want to allow partner reviewers (AWS/GCP) access to the SOC 2 report via trust portal with an allowlist, or provide as a watermarked PDF via secure file share?
- Do we need an NDA for marketplace reviewers specifically, or do we treat them as “customer/prospect reviewer” under standard process?

If we agree on the shape, I’ll update the security packet index page to point to the correct request path and make sure the language matches Aisha’s approved wording.

Thanks,
Olga

—
Olga Petrov
GRC Lead, Redwood Inference


From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>; Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>; Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 28, 2026 at 10:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence links for AWS/GCP Marketplace security review (what we can share + access controls)

Agree with the direction.

Strong preference: no direct links to any confidential evidence in marketplace submission artifacts.

For SOC 2 Type II:
- Provide via trust portal with explicit reviewer allowlist (named individuals or verified partner alias + controlled domain)
- Access duration: 14 days, renewable on request
- Controls: watermark + view-only if portal supports it; if not, watermark + PDF with unique identifier + log access

NDA: treat AWS/GCP reviewers as “partner reviewers” — no NDA required from us if they are reviewing for marketplace listing purposes, BUT we should still use the portal click-through terms and ensure distribution is restricted.

Naomi: can you confirm any product/security constraints on portal approach (e.g., export controls, auditability)?

Aisha

—
Dr. Aisha Rahman
VP Security & Compliance (Exec Sponsor)
Redwood Inference


From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>; Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>; Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 28, 2026 at 11:17 AM PST
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence links for AWS/GCP Marketplace security review (what we can share + access controls)

+1 to portal distribution only.

Constraints / notes:
- We should avoid emailing the SOC2 PDF directly (forwarding risk + no consistent audit trail).
- Use domain allowlisting wherever possible. If AWS/GCP uses an alias (e.g., marketplace-review@), we can allowlist that domain and require verification.
- Require a “reason for access” field in request intake (marketplace security review) so we can report on who we granted access to (this comes up during audits).
- Retention: keep access logs for 12 months minimum (internal), and keep a copy of the exact report version we shared (hash/version control).

I’d also like the evidence index to explicitly say: “Redwood does not publish SOC2 reports publicly; reports are provided via controlled access to verified reviewers.”

Olga — your index is close. One tweak: move bridge letter under “Gated / on request” rather than “Gated” by default; we only issue that if timing requires.

Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance Product Owner
Redwood Inference


From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>; Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>; Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 28, 2026 at 1:02 PM PST
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence links for AWS/GCP Marketplace security review (what we can share + access controls)

This helps a lot for docs.

Two docs-site questions:
1) On the marketplace security docs landing page, can we say “SOC 2 Type II available under NDA/on request” or should we avoid “NDA” entirely and just say “available on request to verified customers/partners”?

2) For the evidence index: do we want a public-facing version (sanitized) that we can link from the marketplace docs, or keep the index internal only and provide it as part of the submission / via email when asked?

If we do a public version, I can add it to the marketplace security packet index with very high-level categories (no tool names, no ticket links, no screenshots).

Alex

—
Alex Martinez
DevEx Lead (Docs/Onboarding)
Redwood Inference


From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>; Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>; Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 28, 2026 at 2:26 PM PST
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence links for AWS/GCP Marketplace security review (what we can share + access controls)

Answers + proposal:

1) Let’s avoid “NDA” language on the docs site. Suggest wording:
“SOC 2 Type II report is available on request to verified customers and partners via controlled access.”
(Aligns with Aisha’s note and doesn’t create a legal commitment we can’t consistently enforce.)

2) Public index: I’d prefer we do NOT publish an “evidence index” publicly. Too easy to turn into a shopping list for attackers and too hard to keep perfectly current.

Instead:
- Public: the marketplace security overview + data handling/retention + audit logs pages
- Submission/partner-only: the evidence index (sanitized, but still not public)

I’ll update the spreadsheet accordingly:
- Remove any references to tooling names, internal ticket IDs, or direct URLs
- Add the explicit line Naomi requested about not publishing the SOC2 report publicly
- Move bridge letter to “on request (as needed)”

Separate note: INT-779 is still open for partner portal access updates (shared alias + permissions). If that slips, we may need a temporary manual grant process owned by GRC.

Olga


From: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>; Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>; Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 28, 2026 at 4:41 PM PST
Subject: Re: SOC 2 evidence links for AWS/GCP Marketplace security review (what we can share + access controls)

Approved.

Final guardrails (please bake into the index + any reviewer notes):
- No pen test reports in marketplace submissions. If requested, exec summary only, shared under controlled access with named recipients.
- No screenshots of internal consoles/tools. Provide narrative descriptions + control statements; evidence is on request.
- Any externally shared SOC2 PDF must be watermarked with recipient + date.

Alex: proceed with the docs language as Olga proposed (no NDA mention).

Olga: once updated, send the sanitized index back to this thread and we’ll use it as the canonical reference for partner review.

Aisha
